A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUPE study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Moved and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulated reinforcement-learning results across 42 tasks, including exploration measurements, ablations, and offline-data robustness experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark and ablation results, revises several reported outcomes, and adds visualizations of sampled skill-policy rollouts.

M1.justification: The trajectory VAE, frozen skills, optimistic reward and skill labeling, high-level online learning, and SUPE (HILP) variant are retained. Algorithm 1 and the method objectives are unchanged; newly disclosed critic-selection details do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same eight domains and 42 main tasks, plus the retained play datasets, offline-data-quality variants, and corruption scenarios. Both antsoccer layouts already appear in v3; selecting arena for sensitivity analysis does not expand overall coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ExPLORe, DBC+JSRL, Trajectory Skills, HILP Skills, and SUPE (HILP), together with the same experiment-specific online-only and ablation variants. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The sensitivity analysis switches its representative soccer task from antsoccer-medium-navigate to antsoccer-arena-navigate. New Figure 5 specifies 16 fixed-latent rollouts per humanoidmaze layout. The additional reward and critic-sweep descriptions do not establish changes to existing training settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds a qualitative analysis of whether frozen skills produce extended navigation, using Figure 5's rollout trajectories. It also revises the antsoccer sensitivity experiment. The ICVF, KL-penalty, exploration-coverage, and offline-data robustness studies were already present.

E5.justification: Both retain interquartile means, 95% stratified-bootstrap confidence intervals, the same stated seed counts, and Table 3's standard errors and one-sided t-tests. Changed confidence-band values do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Substantial curve replacements change antsoccer and cube/scene findings (v3 Figures 16–17; v4 Figures 17–18). SUPE (HILP) becomes clearly strongest on antsoccer-arena, while SUPE's previously positive antsoccer-medium and cube-double-2 returns largely disappear. Sensitivity curves and uncertainty bands also change. These materially revise reported outcomes, although the PDFs do not explain the cause of the replacements.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, VAE objective, pseudo-labeling equations, and appendix reward-estimation mathematics are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: using unlabeled trajectories for both skill pretraining and online high-level learning to accelerate exploration. Their overall contribution and empirical scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds the interpretation that extended frozen-skill rollouts reduce the effective exploration horizon and that different skill-pretraining methods suit different tasks. It narrows the RND-necessity discussion to antmaze and humanoidmaze. The noisy-data failure and frozen-skill limitation already existed.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly identifies antsoccer task-1, documents the one-versus-two-critic sweep, and clarifies the binary whole-task manipulation rewards relative to OGBench's singletask rewards. These improve documentation without establishing changed goals, selected critic settings, or reward functions.

R1.justification: v4 adds unsupervised-skill-discovery references and a focused comparison with observation-only offline RL, including Ma et al. and Song et al. New Appendix D also contains the existing options discussion, which was moved rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: There are focused rewrites of the results discussion, additional setting explanations, and a new Additional Related Work appendix incorporating the relocated options paragraph. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the three-panel skill-rollout Figure 5 and moves the environment montage from v3's appendix Figure 5 to main-text Figure 2. Sensitivity legends, captions, and figure placement are revised, while the general visual format and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility through explicit task, reward, and critic-selection details, and improves interpretation through the rollout visualization and more qualified comparisons. These are limited, concrete gains. The substantial benchmark-result replacements remain insufficiently explained, so they do not establish improved empirical reliability.
